# kubernetes_role_v1

A role contains rules that represent a set of permissions. Permissions are purely additive (there are no "deny" rules).

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `metadata` (Block List) (Required) Standard role's metadata. Exactly one `metadata` block must be present. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--metadata))
- `rule` (Block List) (Required) Rule defining a set of permissions for the role. At least one `rule` block must be present. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Optional

- `bootstrap_connection` (Block List, Max: 1) Connection settings used while this resource is being created, replacing the provider connection configuration in whole. After creation the provider connection configuration will be used. This is to support creating resources when the credentials are not available at plan time (e.g. when creating a cluster and configuring it in the same stack). For managing resources in multiple clusters use aliased providers instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--bootstrap_connection))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique ID for this terraform resource

<a id="nestedblock--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Optional:

- `annotations` (Map of String) An unstructured key value map stored with the role that may be used to store arbitrary metadata. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations
- `generate_name` (String) Prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique name ONLY IF the `name` field has not been provided. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#idempotency
- `labels` (Map of String) Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) the role. May match selectors of replication controllers and services. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/labels
- `name` (String) Name of the role, must be unique. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#names
- `namespace` (String) Namespace defines the space within which name of the role must be unique.

Read-Only:

- `generation` (Number) A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only.
- `resource_version` (String) An opaque value that represents the internal version of this role that can be used by clients to determine when the role has changed. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#concurrency-control-and-consistency
- `uid` (String) The unique in time and space value for this role. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names#uids


<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `api_groups` (Set of String) Name of the APIGroup that contains the resources
- `resources` (Set of String) List of resources that the rule applies to
- `verbs` (Set of String) List of Verbs that apply to ALL the ResourceKinds and AttributeRestrictions contained in this rule

Optional:

- `resource_names` (Set of String) White list of names that the rule applies to


<a id="nestedblock--bootstrap_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bootstrap_connection`

Optional:

- `client_certificate` (String, Sensitive) PEM-encoded client certificate for TLS authentication.
- `client_key` (String, Sensitive) PEM-encoded client certificate key for TLS authentication.
- `cluster_ca_certificate` (String) PEM-encoded root certificates bundle for TLS authentication.
- `config_context` (String) Context to choose from the config file.
- `config_context_auth_info` (String) Authentication info context of the kube config (name of the kubeconfig user, `--user` flag in `kubectl`).
- `config_context_cluster` (String) Cluster context of the kube config (name of the kubeconfig cluster, `--cluster` flag in `kubectl`).
- `config_path` (String) A path to a kube config file.
- `config_paths` (List of String) A list of paths to the kube config files.
- `exec` (Block List, Max: 1) Configuration block to use an exec-based credential plugin, e.g. call an external command to receive user credentials. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--bootstrap_connection--exec))
- `host` (String) The hostname (in form of URI) of the Kubernetes API.
- `insecure` (Boolean) Whether the server should be accessed without verifying the TLS certificate. Defaults to `false`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The password to use for HTTP basic authentication when accessing the Kubernetes API.
- `proxy_url` (String) URL to the proxy to be used for all API requests. URLs with "http", "https", and "socks5" schemes are supported.
- `tls_server_name` (String) Server name passed to the server for SNI and is used in the client to check server certificates against.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Token of your service account.
- `username` (String) The username to use for HTTP basic authentication when accessing the Kubernetes API.

<a id="nestedblock--bootstrap_connection--exec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bootstrap_connection.exec`

Required:

- `api_version` (String) API version to use when decoding the ExecCredentials resource, e.g. `client.authentication.k8s.io/v1`.
- `command` (String) Command to execute.

Optional:

- `args` (List of String) List of arguments to pass when executing the plugin.
- `env` (Map of String, Sensitive) Map of environment variables to set when executing the plugin.





## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kubernetes_role_v1" "example" {
  metadata {
    name = "terraform-example"
    labels = {
      test = "MyRole"
    }
  }

  rule {
    api_groups     = [""]
    resources      = ["pods"]
    resource_names = ["foo"]
    verbs          = ["get", "list", "watch"]
  }
  rule {
    api_groups = ["apps"]
    resources  = ["deployments"]
    verbs      = ["get", "list"]
  }
}
```

## Import

Role can be imported using the namespace and name. Both components must be non-empty, e.g.

```
$ terraform import kubernetes_role_v1.example default/terraform-example
```

Identity imports use `api_version = "rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1"`, `kind = "Role"`,
and `name`. The optional identity `namespace` defaults to `default` when omitted.
An identity with a different `kind` or `api_version` is rejected.

To import a Role that was created with `generateName`, configure `generate_name`
with its original prefix and omit `name`. Configuring `name` instead plans a
replacement.

## Migrating from `kubernetes_role`

With Terraform 1.8 or later, rename the deprecated `kubernetes_role` resource type
to `kubernetes_role_v1`, retain its configuration, and add:

```terraform
moved {
  from = kubernetes_role.example
  to   = kubernetes_role_v1.example
}
```

Terraform records the address change without replacing the Role. A move-only
plan may return exit code 2 with `-detailed-exitcode`, even with no infrastructure
changes. After applying the move, an unchanged configuration plans no changes.

Configurations specifying both `metadata.name` and `metadata.generate_name` are
rejected during planning, including `generate_name = ""`. To keep the existing Role
without replacement:

- If `generate_name = ""`, remove `generate_name`.
- Otherwise, remove `name` and keep `generate_name`. The Role keeps its current
  name; if it is later replaced for another reason, Kubernetes generates a new
  name from the `generate_name` prefix.

Making the other change destroys and recreates the Role.

Existing `kubernetes_role_v1` configurations do not need a `moved` block when
upgrading the provider, including upgrades from provider 2.37.1 before resource
identity was introduced. Omitted `resource_names` defaults to an empty set.
An unset `generate_name` is represented by null rather than the SDKv2 empty string.
Explicit empty metadata maps may require a one-time in-place update. Removing
previously configured labels, annotations, or resource names clears those values.

After upgrading or moving, two further one-time in-place updates may appear, and
neither replaces the Role:

- A Role imported with an earlier provider version may show empty `labels` and
  `annotations` changing to null. Applying it makes no change to the Role.
- A `terraform plan -refresh=false` run immediately after upgrading may show
  `resource_names = []` being added. A plan that refreshes does not show it.

### Null elements in rules

The `api_groups`, `resources`, `resource_names`, and `verbs` sets must not contain
`null` elements. These are rejected during configuration validation, preserving
the SDKv2 provider's rejection during planning. The empty string in
`api_groups = [""]` remains valid and identifies the core API group.
Omitting `resource_names` still defaults to an empty set.

### Null-valued metadata entries

An individual label or annotation value of `null` is rejected during planning.
Earlier SDKv2 versions accepted these entries but silently dropped them from the
Kubernetes object. Remove null-valued entries from the configuration before
upgrading or moving the resource.
